first_impression.reaction: I searched 'something old something new meaning' and later 'something blue ideas'. The intro is short and tells me what's coming, and the Key takeaways are right there. They give me borrowed and blue, but not what old and new actually mean, so I had to keep scrolling for that. Still, I knew I was on the right page fast.

journey.quote: Most couples can recite it before they can say where it came from, and few stop to think about what each line asks of them.
journey.reaction: Nice opener, two lines, then straight into what the page covers. No fluff wall. Good.

journey.quote: The rhyme was first recorded in 1883, as the saying of "some Lancashire friends", and the sixpence line appears in print with it by 1946.
journey.reaction: Interesting, but I asked what it means, not when it was written down. This is the first bullet and it's the history, not the answer.

journey.quote: Blue has long been linked with loyalty and true love, which is why it became the lucky colour for brides.
journey.reaction: There's the blue answer in one line. That's what I wanted.

journey.quote: Something borrowed is lucky when it has already been worn by a happily married bride, and the veil is often singled out as the luckiest piece.
journey.reaction: Okay, borrowed makes sense now. But where's old and new? Two of the four are missing from the summary.

journey.section: 2. Where the rhyme was first printed, and what it means
journey.quote: Something old and something new are where couples make the rhyme their own.
journey.reaction: So old and new don't have a set meaning? Fine if that's honest, but I'd have liked that said up in the takeaways so I didn't have to hunt for it.

journey.section: 6. Something blue ideas that feel considered
journey.quote: Something blue ideas that feel considered
journey.reaction: Heading matches what I typed. Easy to spot while scrolling.

journey.section: 6. Something blue ideas that feel considered

journey.reaction: Love this one, actually. The whole list is short, bold, scannable, and the ideas are a bit nicer than the usual garter-only lists. I'd screenshot this.

journey.quote: Something blue ideas for a wedding overseas:
journey.reaction: Wait, I'm not marrying overseas. The ideas work anywhere though, so the label just makes me wonder if I'm on the wrong page.

journey.quote: When the wedding gown was white, the blue was carried by making the garters blue.
journey.reaction: A whole paragraph of history before the list. On my phone I'd scroll past it to get to the ideas.

journey.quote: A father's or grandfather's cufflinks or tie pin for a partner in a suit.
journey.reaction: Nice that it's not only for brides. Practical list.

journey.section: 9. Carrying heirlooms to a destination wedding
journey.quote: Standard travel insurance policies typically don't cover items stolen from checked baggage on an airline, train or bus.
journey.reaction: Didn't search for this, but it's dated and useful, and it's near the end so it's not in my way.

journey.quote: Something old and something new are personal choices: most couples pick a family heirloom and a piece made or bought for the wedding.
journey.reaction: Good, the FAQ answers the whole question in three lines. If I'd jumped here first I'd be done.

journey.quote: Anything blue you wear or carry. A blue garter is the oldest choice , and a sapphire, blue stitching, a ribbon on the bouquet or blue shoe soles all work.

unanswered_questions: Is there a jump list? On a phone the blue ideas are section 6 of 9 plus an FAQ, and I had to scroll a long way.
Do old and new have any traditional meaning at all, or is it just personal choice? The page implies the second but never says it plainly up top.

turn_offs_found.quote: Something borrowed is lucky when it has already been worn by a happily married bride, and the veil is often singled out as the luckiest piece.
turn_offs_found.why: Key takeaways cover borrowed and blue but skip old and new, so the 'meaning' answer is only half there in the place I read first.

turn_offs_found.quote: When the wedding gown was white, the blue was carried by making the garters blue.
turn_offs_found.why: History paragraph sits ahead of the blue ideas list, so someone searching 'something blue ideas' scrolls past it to get the list.

would_share_with: A friend who's getting married and asked me for something blue ideas; I'd send her section 6

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk through where to marry and how to bring your family pieces with you, tell us your date, your guest list and the feeling you want.
cta_reaction.why: I came for a quick answer, not to plan anything. It's at the very end and soft, so it didn't bother me. I might tap the magazine link though.

top_3_changes: Add a takeaways bullet saying old and new are personal choices (a family heirloom and a piece made or bought for the day), so all four meanings are in the summary.
Put the blue ideas list before the history paragraph in section 6, and drop 'for a wedding overseas' from the list label since the ideas work anywhere.
Add a short jump list after the takeaways so phone readers can get to the blue, borrowed or sixpence sections quickly.
